rot.perpetualCheck.ideia.ex1.e1: Perpetual check: let us think from White's side, with White to move. Game TimeAndChance × BonesSerg, on Lichess. Black has the extra bishop and knight.
rot.perpetualCheck.ideia.ex1.e2: Look at the black king: only it defends the pawn on f7, and the rook on f1 stands behind your queen, on the same file.
rot.perpetualCheck.ideia.ex1.p: Find the strongest move for White.
rot.perpetualCheck.ideia.ex1.certo: The queen captures the pawn on f7 with check. The king cannot capture it: the rook on f1 defends it.
rot.perpetualCheck.ideia.ex1.revela: The move is the queen to f7: it captures the pawn with check, defended by the rook on f1.
rot.perpetualCheck.ideia.ex1.err.e1e4.1: The rook captures the bishop on e4.
rot.perpetualCheck.ideia.ex1.err.e1e4.2: The knight recaptures on e4 and attacks your queen and the pawn on g5. It now also defends f6, and Black is a rook and a knight up.
rot.perpetualCheck.ideia.ex1.err.e1e4.3: Back to the position: you are worse. Look for checks the black king cannot avoid.
rot.perpetualCheck.ideia.ex1.fora: That move changes nothing: Black stays two pieces up. Look for a check.
rot.perpetualCheck.ideia.ex1.volta: Try again: start with the pawn on f7, which only the king defends.
rot.perpetualCheck.ideia.ex1.l1: The king only has h8: g7 and f8 belong to the queen.
rot.perpetualCheck.ideia.ex1.l3: The queen gives check on f6, defended by the pawn on g5. The king only has g8: g7 belongs to the queen, and h7 is occupied by the pawn.
rot.perpetualCheck.ideia.ex1.l4: The king goes back to g8.
rot.perpetualCheck.ideia.ex1.l5: The queen goes back to f7 with check, and everything repeats.
rot.perpetualCheck.ideia.ex1.l6: This is perpetual check: checks your opponent cannot avoid, and the position repeats until the draw. In positions like this, when you are worse and the enemy king has no shelter, look for those checks.
rot.perpetualCheck.ideia.ex2.e1: Stalemate: White again, in the game Evans × Reshevsky, United States championship, New York 1963. Black is a knight up and threatens mate: the queen goes to g2 or h2.
rot.perpetualCheck.ideia.ex2.e2: Look at your side: the king on h1 has no square, and the pawns on b4, e4, f3 and h4 are blocked. Without the queen and the rook, White would have no move.
rot.perpetualCheck.ideia.ex2.p: Find the strongest move for White.
rot.perpetualCheck.ideia.ex2.certo: The queen gives check on g8 and gives itself up.
rot.perpetualCheck.ideia.ex2.revela: The move is the queen to g8, with check: you give up the queen.
rot.perpetualCheck.ideia.ex2.alt.c8h8.1: The queen on h8 also draws: after the king captures it, the rook gives checks without end. In the game, the queen went to g8.
rot.perpetualCheck.ideia.ex2.err.c8f5.1: The queen gives check on f5.
rot.perpetualCheck.ideia.ex2.err.c8f5.2: The knight goes to g6 and blocks the check. The queen has no more repeating checks, and Black gives mate.
rot.perpetualCheck.ideia.ex2.err.c8f5.3: Back to the position: your king and your pawns have no move. See what happens if the queen and the rook leave the board.
rot.perpetualCheck.ideia.ex2.err.f7g7.1: The rook captures the pawn on g7 with check, but the black queen can capture it.
rot.perpetualCheck.ideia.ex2.err.f7g7.2: The black queen captures the rook. Your queen is still on the board, so there is no stalemate, and Black is far ahead in material.
rot.perpetualCheck.ideia.ex2.err.f7g7.3: Back to the position: your king and your pawns have no move. See what happens if the queen and the rook leave the board.
rot.perpetualCheck.ideia.ex2.fora: That move does not stop the mate on g2. Remember: your king and your pawns have no move.
rot.perpetualCheck.ideia.ex2.volta: Try again: start by giving up the queen with check.
rot.perpetualCheck.ideia.ex2.l0: The black king has to capture it: if it runs to g6 or h6, the queen and the rook give mate on g7.
rot.perpetualCheck.ideia.ex2.l1: The king captures the queen on g8.
rot.perpetualCheck.ideia.ex2.l2: The rook captures the pawn on g7 with check and offers itself: if it is captured, White has no move.
rot.perpetualCheck.ideia.ex2.l3: The king runs to f8. The rook follows the king.
rot.perpetualCheck.ideia.ex2.l6: Check again, on e7. The rook does not leave the black king.
rot.perpetualCheck.ideia.ex2.l7: The king captures the rook, and White is stalemated: the game is drawn.
rot.perpetualCheck.ideia.ex2.l8: In the game, the draw came right after the check on g7. In positions like this, when your king and your pawns have no move, giving up the pieces you have left leads to stalemate.
rot.perpetualCheck.demos.repete.1: Perpetual check: White, in the game babakabd × SMestanov, on Lichess. Black is a bishop up and threatens mate: the queen captures the pawn on g2, defended by the rook on g8.
rot.perpetualCheck.demos.repete.2: Defending g2 looks natural. But the black king is in the corner, and your queen reaches f6 with check.
rot.perpetualCheck.demos.repete.3: The queen captures the pawn on f6 with check. The king has no square: g8 is occupied by the rook, and g7 belongs to the queen. Only the rook can block.
rot.perpetualCheck.demos.repete.4: The rook blocks the check on g7. Now it no longer defends g2.
rot.perpetualCheck.demos.repete.5: The queen gives check on d8, along the eighth rank.
rot.perpetualCheck.demos.repete.6: Only the rook can block again: it goes back to g8.
rot.perpetualCheck.demos.repete.7: The queen goes back to f6 with check. The position repeats: it is perpetual check.
rot.perpetualCheck.demos.repete.8: In positions like this, the check comes before your opponent's threat, as in the counterattack: while you give check, the black queen never reaches g2.
rot.perpetualCheck.demos.entrega.1: Stalemate: now with Black, in the game Gelfand × Kramnik, Candidates match, Sanghi Nagar 1994. You are two pawns down, and the white queen attacks the pawn on f6.
rot.perpetualCheck.demos.entrega.2: Look at your side: the pawns on a6, f6 and h6 are blocked, and the one on g7 is pinned by the rook on e7. The g6 square belongs to the pawns on f5 and h5.
rot.perpetualCheck.demos.entrega.3: The queen goes to c1, toward the white king, and leaves the rook on d8 undefended.
rot.perpetualCheck.demos.entrega.4: The white queen captures the rook on d8. Now it also takes g8 and h8 from your king: your king and your pawns have no move.
rot.perpetualCheck.demos.entrega.5: The queen gives check on h1. The white king only has g3.
rot.perpetualCheck.demos.entrega.7: The queen gives check on h2 and gives itself up: the king can only capture it.
rot.perpetualCheck.demos.entrega.8: The king captures the queen, and Black is stalemated: the game is drawn.
rot.perpetualCheck.demos.entrega.9: In the game, Gelfand did not capture the rook, and the game was drawn. In positions like this, with your king and your pawns stuck, giving up your last piece leads to stalemate.
rot.perpetualCheck.demos.excecao.1: Perpetual check: now with Black, in the game HikaruMcNamara × hursh_a6_b5, on Lichess. White has two queens against yours.
rot.perpetualCheck.demos.excecao.2: Your queen can give checks on h4 and h3, and the white king cannot escape them: perpetual check is at hand. Before accepting the draw, look at the white king's squares.
rot.perpetualCheck.demos.excecao.3: The queen gives check on h5. The white king only has g7: g8 and h8 are occupied by the white queens, and g6 and h6 belong to your queen.
rot.perpetualCheck.demos.excecao.4: The queen gives mate on g6, defended by the pawn on f7. Your king on e7 covers f8, and the white queens occupy g8 and h8.
rot.perpetualCheck.demos.excecao.5: In positions like this, perpetual check is the defense of the side that is worse. Before accepting the draw, look for mate: here it was there.
rot.perpetualCheck.pratica.valeAqui.enun: Game genghis_khannn × sms0, on Lichess. White has two queens and threatens your king. Perpetual check is at hand: the queen gives check on g1. Does it work here? Play as Black.
rot.perpetualCheck.pratica.valeAqui.fim: The queen gave check on f2, the king went to h3, and the rook gave mate on h1. Perpetual check drew; here there was mate. Before accepting the draw, look for mate.
The queen gives check on g1, and the white king runs. The checks draw, but here there was mate. Look for the check that leaves the king a single square.
The queen gives check on c3, but the king goes to g2 and threatens to capture the rook on f1. After that, the white queens reach your king. Look for the check that leaves the king a single square.
The rook gives check on g1, but the king runs to f3, and the checks do not lead to mate. Look for the queen check that leaves the king a single square.
rot.perpetualCheck.pratica.torre.enuncia: Game werbini × Korchnoiiiii13, on Lichess. Black is ahead in material and threatens to capture the knight on e3 with the rook: leaving c3, the rook opens the diagonal of the bishop on a5, which then gives check. Play as White and look for the draw.
rot.perpetualCheck.pratica.torre.fim: The rook gave check on g4 and on g3, squares defended by the knight and by the pawn on h2: the king cannot capture it. In positions like this, the rook can give perpetual check too.
rot.perpetualCheck.pratica.torre.err.g1g: The rook captures the pawn on g7, but gives no check: the rook on c3 captures the knight on e3 and uncovers the check of the bishop on a5. Look for a check.
rot.perpetualCheck.pratica.torre.err.g1f: The rook gives check on f1, but the black king goes to e4, and the checks are over. Look for the check where the king cannot capture the rook.
rot.perpetualCheck.pratica.torre.err.e3g: The knight gives check on g2 and escapes the attack, but the black king goes to e4 and escapes the checks, and Black stays ahead in material. Look for the check with the rook.
rot.perpetualCheck.pratica.torre.err2.g4: The rook captures the pawn on g7, but gives no check: the rook on c3 captures the knight on e3 and uncovers the check of the bishop on a5. Look for a check.
rot.perpetualCheck.pratica.troitsky.enun: Game Troitsky × Vogt, 1896. Black threatens mate on g2, and almost all your pieces on the kingside are stuck. Play as White and look for the draw.
rot.perpetualCheck.pratica.troitsky.fim: The rook traded itself for the one on d8, and the queen gave check on d1. If the black queen captures, White is stalemated: bishop, f2 pawn and knight pinned, rook stuck. Otherwise, you capture the black queen.
The queen captures the pawn on c7 with check, but the bishop on b6 captures it, and the mate on g2 remains. Start by moving the rook on d1 out of the queen's way.
rot.perpetualCheck.pratica.troitsky.err2: The checks run out, and Black gives mate. Look for the check where the black queen captures yours and leaves White with no move.
